newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan March industrial output up 10.01 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan March industrial output up 10.01 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's industrial output in March rose 10.01 percent compared to March 1996, the economics ministry said on Tuesday.
The growth was the highest in two years, and was far above an average forecast of 5.57 percent rise that resulted from an April 18 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.

The finance ministry attributed the rise to companies rushing to make up for lost production following a new national holiday in February which reduced the number of working days that month to only 17.5.
"The high growth is somewhat misleading due to the extra February holiday this year," ministry's chief statistician Chang Yao-chung told reporters.
"But the high growth does indicate a stable recovery in the economy," Chang said.
The manufacturing index, including metals, machinery, information electronics, chemical and consumer products, rose a whopping 11.45 percent in March from the same month in 1996.
Real estate and construction industry output dropped 17.12 percent year-on-year, but was up 38.04 percent from February.
"The long-sluggish real estate industry is showing signs of rebounding, and clear recovery of the property market will be seen in the third quarter," Chang said.
Chang said a year-on-year rise of 83.75 percent in the land area for which construction firms have sought development permits also indicated that the sector was on its way to a rebound.
